cloze.prompt: The {{blank}} is the whole set of people or items being investigated.
cloze.explanation: A population is the full group of interest.

cloze.prompt: A census observes or measures {{blank}} member of the defined population.
cloze.explanation: A census includes every member.

cloze.prompt: A {{blank}} is used to draw conclusions about a wider population.
cloze.explanation: A sample uses only part of the population.

cloze.prompt: Data that have not yet been processed or summarised are called {{blank}} data.
cloze.explanation: Raw data are the original observations.

cloze.prompt: An individual item that could be selected is a sampling {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: Sampling unit refers to a person or item.

cloze.prompt: A numbered list of eligible sampling units can form a sampling {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: A sampling frame identifies the units from which selection occurs.

cloze.prompt: In a simple random sample of size n, every possible {{blank}} of size n is equally likely.
cloze.explanation: The definition concerns possible groups of n, not only individual chances.

cloze.prompt: When generating random numbers without replacement, {{blank}} repeated numbers.
cloze.explanation: Each selected unit must appear only once.

cloze.prompt: When reading an unrestricted random-digit source, {{blank}} numbers outside the numbered frame.
cloze.explanation: Out-of-range rejection matters for unrestricted sources, not generators constrained to 1 to N.

cloze.prompt: Systematic sampling takes units at {{blank}} intervals from an ordered list.
cloze.explanation: An ordered list and regular interval are essential.

cloze.prompt: For systematic sampling, the first position is selected at {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: A random start is required.

cloze.prompt: In stratified sampling, the population is separated into mutually exclusive {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: Strata are distinct population groups.

cloze.prompt: Within each stratum, the members are selected {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: Random selection within groups distinguishes stratified from quota sampling.

cloze.prompt: The number selected from each stratum is proportional to the {{blank}} of that stratum in the population.
cloze.explanation: Proportional allocation reflects each group's relative size.

cloze.prompt: In quota sampling, interviewers recruit until each group {{blank}} is filled.
cloze.explanation: Targets are filled without random selection within groups.

cloze.prompt: Opportunity sampling selects eligible people who are readily {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: Selection is by availability at the time of the study.

cloze.prompt: Different random samples can give different conclusions because of sampling {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: Different subsets contain different observations.

cloze.prompt: Data recording categories rather than measured numerical amounts are {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: Qualitative values describe categories.

cloze.prompt: Numerical amounts from counts or measurements are {{blank}} data.
cloze.explanation: Quantitative data measure or count amounts.

cloze.prompt: The number of pupils in a class is a {{blank}} variable.
cloze.explanation: Counts take separate possible values.

cloze.prompt: Time taken to complete a race is modelled as a {{blank}} variable.
cloze.explanation: Time can take any value in an interval, regardless of recorded rounding.

cloze.prompt: A frequency table collecting observations into class {{blank}} is grouped.
cloze.explanation: Grouped data use intervals.

cloze.prompt: The upper and lower values defining a class are its class {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: Class boundaries define interval ends.

cloze.prompt: Class width is upper boundary {{blank}} lower boundary.
cloze.explanation: Subtract the class boundaries.

cloze.prompt: Class midpoint is the {{blank}} of the two class boundaries.
cloze.explanation: Midpoint = (lower + upper)/2.

cloze.prompt: For a study concerned with all 320 Year 12 pupils, those 320 pupils form the {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: The population is defined by the investigation, not by the eventual subset surveyed.

cloze.prompt: Even if every pupil is measured in a census, {{blank}} errors can still occur.
cloze.explanation: A census avoids sampling variation from choosing a subset, but it does not prevent measurement or recording errors.

cloze.prompt: Measuring 35 randomly chosen trees out of 500 produces a {{blank}}, not a census.
cloze.explanation: A sample is the subset observed; the 500 trees are the target population.

cloze.prompt: The original unsummarised measurements in a scientist's notebook are {{blank}} data.
cloze.explanation: Individual measurements before summaries are raw data; calculated means are not.

cloze.prompt: When whole classrooms are selected from a list of classrooms, each classroom is a sampling {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: The sampling unit is what can be selected; here that is a classroom, not a pupil.

cloze.prompt: An employee register that omits eligible workers is an incomplete sampling {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: A sampling frame identifies units available for selection; omitted workers have no chance of being chosen from this register.

cloze.prompt: Selection by an impartial chance procedure rather than the researcher's judgement is {{blank}} sampling.
cloze.explanation: Random selection is chance-based; its precise probabilities depend on the sampling design.

cloze.prompt: An interviewer choosing people to fit personal preferences is not using {{blank}} sampling.
cloze.explanation: Personal preference is not a chance-based method; random sampling requires an impartial random process.

cloze.prompt: In a survey divided into year groups, one complete year-group subgroup is a {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: A stratum is one group in a partition of the population, not a single sampled person.

cloze.prompt: The singular name for one population subgroup within a stratified design is {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: Stratum is singular; strata refers to two or more of the population groups.

cloze.prompt: Filling a quota by approaching willing people is {{blank}} selection within each group.
cloze.explanation: Quota sampling uses fixed group targets but does not randomly select people within those groups.

cloze.prompt: Asking the next willing customers at a shop entrance without setting group targets is {{blank}} sampling.
cloze.explanation: People are recruited because they are available; without group targets this is not quota sampling.

cloze.prompt: If some eligible residents have no chance of being approached, the survey may suffer {{blank}} bias.
cloze.explanation: Unequal or missing inclusion opportunities can systematically distort the people represented.

cloze.prompt: Leaving particular eligible groups off a register can introduce selection {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: An incomplete frame can exclude groups systematically even if the draw from that frame is random.

cloze.prompt: A {{blank}} sample resembles its target population in characteristics relevant to the investigation.
cloze.explanation: Representativeness concerns relevant population characteristics, not just the number sampled.

cloze.prompt: Matching an age-group proportion alone does not guarantee a sample is {{blank}} for every outcome.
cloze.explanation: Matching one characteristic cannot guarantee agreement in all other characteristics or behaviours.

cloze.prompt: Two different well-chosen random samples can have different means due to sampling {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: Different subsets can yield different statistics even when the sampling procedure is valid.

cloze.prompt: If 600 numbered records are sampled systematically using 40 positions with a fixed gap, the sampling {{blank}} is 15.
cloze.explanation: For this exact integer case, the systematic interval is 600 ÷ 40 = 15.

cloze.prompt: The constant gap between selected positions in systematic sampling is the sampling {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: An interval is the fixed step along the ordered list, used after choosing a random start.

cloze.prompt: If one stratum contains 20% of the population, proportional allocation assigns it {{blank}}% of the sample.
cloze.explanation: Proportional allocation uses the same population share for the target sample share; 20% stays 20%.

cloze.prompt: A bus route identified by the code 17 is a {{blank}} category, not a measured numerical amount.
cloze.explanation: A route number is a label even though digits are used, so it is categorical or qualitative data.

cloze.prompt: The number of tickets sold at a cinema each hour is {{blank}} data.
cloze.explanation: A count is a numerical amount; a route or ticket category code may instead be qualitative.

cloze.prompt: The result of rolling a standard six-sided die is a {{blank}} numerical variable.
cloze.explanation: The result takes one of six distinct possible numerical values rather than any value in an interval.

cloze.prompt: A length rounded to the nearest centimetre is still modelled as a {{blank}} variable.
cloze.explanation: The underlying measured length can vary continuously even though recorded values are rounded.

cloze.prompt: After values are grouped into class intervals, the original exact measurements cannot normally be {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: Grouped frequencies tell how many values fall into each interval but lose the individual exact observations.

cloze.prompt: For heights recorded to the nearest centimetre, the upper class boundary for the class 150–159 cm is {{blank}} cm.
cloze.explanation: Measurements recorded as 159 cm can represent true lengths up to 159.5 cm, the upper boundary.

cloze.prompt: A class with lower boundary 12.5 and upper boundary 17.5 has width {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: Class width equals upper boundary minus lower boundary: 17.5 − 12.5 = 5.

cloze.prompt: For the interval 10 ≤ x < 20, the class midpoint is {{blank}}.
cloze.explanation: The midpoint is the mean of the two boundaries: (10 + 20)/2 = 15.
